title: Multisensory Gamma Entrainment
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from a single healthy participant (23 years old, male) during multisensory stimulation designed to investigate gamma-band brain entrainment. The study examined three distinct sensory conditions: auditory stimulation (40 Hz modulated 5 kHz tone), visual stimulation (20 Hz flickering light), and combined audio-visual stimulation, each lasting 40 seconds. The research aims to characterize how different sensory modalities drive synchronized brain oscillations, with potential implications for understanding sensory-driven gamma entrainment mechanisms relevant to neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease. Note: This is a single-subject study.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded from 19 monopolar channels using the standard 10/20 system referenced to earlobes at 500 Hz sampling rate with electrode impedance maintained below 20 kOhm. Auditory stimulation consisted of a 40 Hz amplitude-modulated 5 kHz carrier tone (4% duty cycle) delivered via speakers at 50 cm distance. Visual stimulation was a 20 Hz flickering white LED array at 50 cm distance with 50% duty cycle. Preprocessing followed Makoto's pipeline including highpass filtering (>1 Hz), line noise removal, bad channel rejection and interpolation, average re-referencing, Artifact Subspace Reconstruction, independent component analysis, dipole fitting, and bad dipole rejection using EEGLab.
